surface: The intl-datetime editor, a native date and time input over the cell: opening it, typing a new date, Enter committing it, and Escape cancelling a second edit.

steps.note: Enter opens the editor on the Datetime cell (`06/10/2024, 09:30:00`) and focuses its native `datetime-local` input, which holds 2024-06-10T09:30:00. Required: the control, in the reader's words (NVDA `date edit`, with Firefox `date edit, multi line`; VoiceOver `Month stepper`). `time` is not a synonym, because the Time column's name would satisfy it. Finding: VoiceOver says nothing when the editor opens, on both browsers, and reads the stepper only when it opens a second time (the reopen step), as for the date and time editors.

Four digits fill the month and the day of the input in Chromium and Firefox; the year and the time keep their values, so the new value is 2024-01-01T09:30:00. WebKit's input does not move to the next segment, so both pairs land in the month and the commit gives 01/10/2024: on VoiceOver with WebKit the groups of the next steps that name the typed date fail for the input, not for the reading. Nothing is required here: a reader speaks a segment's new value in its own words.

Enter commits the value and moves the selection one row down (enterMoves), to the next row's Datetime, drawn as `01/05/2024, 10:15:00`. Required: that cell's date and its row. NVDA says a date as `01 slash 05 slash 2024`, the synonym. Finding: the focus stays on the closed input, so no reader reads the cell: NVDA with Chromium reads the year segment, NVDA with Firefox says nothing, and VoiceOver reads a stepper of the hidden input (`1 month stepper` with WebKit, `2024 Year stepper` with Chromium).
ArrowUp moves to the edited cell, drawn as `01/01/2024, 09:30:00` (`01/10/2024` in WebKit, see the typing step); the arrow key takes the focus from the closed input to the cell.
The editor opens again, on the new value, and every reader names the control this time.
Escape closes the editor without a change. Finding: no reader says anything, on any browser, and the focus stays on the closed input, as the commit leaves it.
